chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Amiri, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the price of the dog that does not hunt, so he said: 'It is good (halal/permissible), and as for the hunting dog, there is no harm (in its price).'.

key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Good / Permissible / Halal sustenance or value

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the price and trade of non-hunting dogs versus hunting dogs?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the commercial valuation of dogs by distinguishing between non-hunting dogs, whose price is deemed 'suh't' (permissible or good), and hunting dogs, which are also acceptable in trade. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that the utility of the animal determines its marketability, countering earlier views that might have considered all dogs impure or worthless. The term 'suh't' here implies that the price is not negligible, affirming their status as valid commodities in Islamic commerce.
